approach: Root cause: defaults.toml records no stance on tool version pins or on checks that lean on ambient tools, so the reader had to ask in jobs 20261016-005805-p806 and 20261025-183644-t67q. Fix it there. (1) Append two entries to defaults.toml in the real shape (`id`, `statement`, `applies_to`, `source`; `Default` has `deny_unknown_fields`, defaults.rs:16-23, so the brief's `classes` and `text` would not parse). `DefaultsModel::render` (defaults.rs:58-72) shows the reader only the first sentence of each statement (`first_sentence`, defaults.rs:77-83), so each first sentence carries the whole stance and its scope. Scope (answers findings 2 and 5): `version-pins` covers tool version pins in athena.toml (`agents.claude_version`, athena.toml:59, and `[tools.*] version`, athena.toml:154), not Cargo requirements (Cargo.toml:38-46 floats on purpose); `hermetic-checks` covers checks run by Athena's check runner, which already runs `env_clear().envs(ctx.env)` (checks.rs:532-536), not unit tests that spawn git from the test process. Later sentences hold the carve-outs and the D154 command name for the producer and verifier, who get full statements through `get`. (2) Prove it on the reader's real input (answers finding 3): the reader is built by `reader_system_prompt` (reading.rs:241-253) from the whole unfiltered `jc.defaults.render()`, assigned to `AgentInvocation.system_prompt` (reading.rs:444). A new test in run_pin_tests.rs drives `Athena::ask` and reads that field through the existing `Tweak`. A data-level test in defaults.rs checks the same phrases on the parsed file and on the rendered line. (3) Measure first, then set the budget (answers finding 6): add the entries, read the reader size from the failing budget test, then set `BudgetSet::Reader` to the next multiple of 50 above it. Estimate: about 494 added bytes, about 165 tokens, 1998 to about 2163, so 2_200; the producer replaces this with the measured figure. Replace the literal 2000 at run_pin_tests.rs:1625 with `BudgetSet::Reader.budget()`, as the verifier line above it already does (:1621). (4) Update the `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md. It is not a listed deliverable (finding 1), but `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (budgets.rs:125-129) fails without it. The file is `include_str!`ed at briefs.rs:1411, and the criterion-6 test run needs the edit. The 4-digit to 4-digit change keeps its byte length. (5) Append D181 to docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG bullet, both naming the root cause. `version = 1` stays, for reasons recorded in D181 (answers finding 4).

decisions.choice: Scope version-pins to tool version pins in athena.toml, in the first sentence: "Tool version pins in athena.toml stay exact and are never auto-floated; only the person running Athena bumps one, through one explicit command that sets the pin to the installed version." A later sentence names `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` for the Claude Code pin (D154; xtask/src/main.rs:16, 686) and says Cargo dependency requirements and Cargo.lock are outside the default. applies_to = code, config, build (criterion 1).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Unscoped, the sentence reads as a rule against the repository's own floating Cargo requirements (Cargo.toml:38-46). Reader.md:17 tells the reader to record every applicable standing default as a criterion without asking, so a broad default would add false criteria to ordinary code jobs. The introspection's own pins are the athena.toml ones, and "sets the pin to the installed version" only fits installed tools. The scope sits in the first sentence, the one the reader sees; the test pins "Tool version pins in athena.toml" on the rendered line, so it cannot drift out.

Later sentences: a fallback taken without that record is a failure, and unit tests that start git or cargo from the test process are outside the default. applies_to = code, config, build, with `tests` dropped.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The runner already clears the environment and passes `ctx.env` (checks.rs:532-536), so the rule is about what the athena.toml checks and gates need. Many unit tests spawn git from PATH (run_pin_tests.rs:109-135 builds a repo with git), so the unscoped wording would flag them. Code, config and build are where a check is defined or changed; `tests` would pull the rule into every test-writing request. Criterion 2 names no classes, so this is allowed.

demonstrations.method: The new test `the_reader_system_prompt_carries_the_pin_and_hermetic_check_defaults` in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs builds `repo(&config(true))`, which commits the real defaults.toml (run_pin_tests.rs:121-123). It builds Athena with `athena_with` and a `Tweak` that records `system_prompt` and `user_prompt` of every `Role::Reader` invocation. It calls `athena.ask("The pinned Claude Code version no longer matches the installed one, so every job stops.", &Quiet)`: the same shape as the p806 request, with no governance path name and no job id. It asserts one reader invocation. Its system prompt must contain `- version-pins [code, config, build]: Tool version pins in athena.toml stay exact and are never auto-floated`, `- hermetic-checks [code, config, build]: A check run by Athena's check runner never depends on inherited environment or ambient tools`, and "do not ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise" (reader.md:17). Its brief must contain the request text. Limit: the fake reader does not read the prompt, so this shows the reader's input answers the pin question and the frame tells it to apply standing defaults unasked. It does not show that a live model then skips the question; no live run is demonstrated. The p806 request text is not in the snapshot, so the stand-in is a request of the same shape.
demonstrations.observes: The reader's actual system prompt, as production composes it, carries both stances in the lines the reader loads, next to the rule that standing defaults apply without a question.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the version-pins entry the reader's system prompt has no `- version-pins [` line, so the assertion fails. With a pin-deadlock request and no stated stance, the reader's input would leave the policy open and it would have to ask, as in job 20261016-005805-p806.
